authorship: Same assistant controlled claims and source-reading references; not independent review or authentic analyst entries.

source_cautions.gh-february-2024: The retained combined section has inconsistent incident dates and durations. No claim uses those inconsistent facts; no source text was repaired.

claims.claim: Some Git backend requests failed or timed out during the January 9 incident.
claims.rationale: The impact paragraph includes the Git backend among services experiencing timed-out requests and failures.

claims.claim: The January 9 incident caused no Git backend request failures or timeouts.
claims.rationale: The paragraph explicitly includes Git backend failures and timeouts.

claims.claim: The January 9 incident affected more than one thousand customers.
claims.rationale: The excerpt gives percentages of requests, not the number of affected customers; it neither establishes nor rules out this customer count.

claims.claim: Operational problems with compute and storage resources disrupted Codespace creation and resumption on January 21.
claims.rationale: The report attributes Codespaces creation and resumption issues to operational compute and storage problems.

claims.claim: Compute and storage resources operated normally throughout the January 21 Codespaces incident.
claims.rationale: The report explicitly describes operational issues with both resource types.

claims.claim: A storage failure began before the compute problems in the January 21 incident.
claims.rationale: The excerpt does not establish the sequence of compute and storage problems. Regional recovery timing does not settle their order.

claims.claim: Changes were deployed to remediate the January 31 blocking issue, alongside improvements to testing and monitoring.
claims.rationale: The remediation paragraph explicitly describes deployed changes and testing/monitoring steps.

claims.claim: No changes were deployed to remediate the January 31 blocking issue.
claims.rationale: The remediation paragraph explicitly states that changes were deployed.

claims.claim: Restarting load balancers restored service during the January 31 incident.
claims.rationale: The report describes remediation changes but does not say whether a restart restored service. The underlying recovery mechanism is not settled.

claims.claim: The February 26 incident delayed Webhooks, GitHub Actions and UI updates.
claims.rationale: The February 26 paragraph explicitly lists delays in all three.

claims.claim: The February 26 incident lost customer data.
claims.rationale: The report explicitly says no data was lost during that incident.

claims.claim: The February 26 incident affected more than one thousand customers.
claims.rationale: The affected service types are listed, but the customer count is neither supplied nor bounded.

claims.claim: Capacity constraints in the job queue and a failure of automated failover contributed to the February 26 incident.
claims.rationale: The report relates the February 26 incident to both capacity constraints and automated failover failure.

claims.claim: Automated failover worked normally during the February 26 incident.
claims.rationale: The February 26 paragraph explicitly identifies failure of automated failover; successful failover in the other incident does not establish this claim.

claims.claim: A memory leak caused the job-queue capacity constraints on February 26.
claims.rationale: The report identifies capacity constraints, but does not establish or exclude a memory leak as their underlying cause.

claims.claim: A correction at 11:21 UTC allowed the backlog to drain before full restoration at 11:27 UTC during the February 29 incident.
claims.rationale: The February 29 paragraph describes the correction, subsequent backlog processing and full restoration in that order.

claims.claim: The successful February 29 failover at 09:32 UTC kept services healthy for the rest of the incident without a later backlog increase.
claims.rationale: The report describes a later improper restoration to primary that significantly increased queued jobs before correction and final recovery.

claims.claim: Adding new machines cleared the February 29 backlog.
claims.rationale: The excerpt reports a correction and later capacity improvements, but does not establish or rule out adding machines as the mechanism that cleared this backlog.

claims.claim: The March 15 permissions regression caused failures in Codespaces, Actions and Pages.
claims.rationale: The March 15 paragraph explicitly lists failures in the three services.

claims.claim: GitHub Pages experienced no failures during the March 15 incident.
claims.rationale: The March 15 paragraph explicitly includes Pages among services with failures.

claims.claim: The March 15 incident lost customer repository data.
claims.rationale: The excerpt describes failures and rollback, but neither establishes nor rules out repository data loss.

claims.claim: An inadvertent network-configuration deployment to the wrong environment caused the March 11 service degradation.
claims.rationale: The March 11 paragraph attributes degradation to an inadvertent deployment to the wrong environment.

claims.claim: The network-configuration deployment that caused the March 11 incident went to its intended environment.
claims.rationale: The report explicitly says the configuration was deployed to the wrong environment.

claims.claim: A database engineer approved the network-configuration deployment that caused the March 11 incident.
claims.rationale: The excerpt does not name the approver or their role; the incorrect deployment target does not settle approval.

claims.claim: Manual correction of configuration data enabled full rollback and service restoration by 00:48 UTC in the March 11 incident.
claims.rationale: The report explicitly connects manual configuration correction with successful full rollback and restoration.

claims.claim: Full rollback completed in every data center without manual intervention during the March 11 incident.
claims.rationale: Rollback failed in one data center and manual intervention was required before full rollback succeeded.

claims.claim: An on-call database engineer performed the manual configuration correction during the March 11 incident.
claims.rationale: The report establishes manual intervention, but does not name the operator or their role.
